Asked on MSNBC how Democrats would end the war in Iran if they win in November, Maryland Senator Angela Alsobrooks insisted the exit strategy is solely President Trump's responsibility because he initiated the conflict.

The Bright Side:
Alsobrooks' voting record proves consistent resistance to unauthorized executive conflict in Iran, using available legislative war powers to register formal congressional opposition.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is Logical (HOW): passing resolutions does not physically stop military deployments without enforcing the power of the purse. Congress baits constitutional duty and switches to rhetorical exemption.

Social Physics Analysis:
Alsobrooks runs a Smart Selfish maneuver: using past votes as a pretext to deflect hard questions about executive accountability. Instead of leveraging purse strings, she projects complete responsibility onto Trump.

The Trajectory: The Path of Fall into Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil as legislative duty decays into passive partisan deflection.

The Unavoidable Truth: Congress holds the constitutional power of the purse to halt unapproved foreign wars.
The Unavoidable Lie: Casting symbolic roll-call votes fully discharges a legislator's duty to end a conflict.

Alethekanon:
Legislative oversight cannot be reduced to a punch-clock chore. Casting votes against war while declaring your job finished abdicates Article I co-equal governance.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to watch leaders treat war as an electoral talking point. When lives are on the line overseas, citizens need brave statesmen building real pathways to peace, not politicians washing their hands.

Brothekanon:
Saying 'I voted no, so my job is done' is peak Washington energy. You're a US Senator, bro, not an intern clocking out at five. If you want the war to stop, cut off the money.
